title: `celery status` dumps a Python traceback when the broker is down
title_original: Fix#9722 friendly status errors for CLI
text_original:
### Summary

Thanks @harshang03 for the awesome work on #10118! The UX improvement for CLI broker errors is fantastic and much needed.

I noticed that Codecov reported some missing coverage and @auvipy requested additional tests. Since the PR hasn't been updated in about a month, I went ahead and added the missing unit tests to cover the remaining `try...except` blocks to help get this over the finish line.

### What was added
Added unit tests to simulate `OperationalError` and unexpected exceptions for the following commands, ensuring the `handle_remote_command_error` is triggered correctly:
- [x] `celery inspect <command>` 
- [x] `celery control <command>` (broadcast)
- [x] `celery events` (covering the `_run_evcam` and `_run_evtop` paths)

---
issue https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/9722
text_rewritten: Running `celery status` against a cluster whose broker is not reachable prints a raw Python traceback and exits with a generic failure code. Operators cannot tell whether they mistyped the broker URL, whether the broker is down, or whether they hit a bug in the tool. A command that cannot reach the cluster should report that as an unavailable service: exit with the platform's EX_UNAVAILABLE status, print one line naming the underlying reason, and print no traceback. A reachable broker with no workers must keep the unavailable outcome it already reports, and a healthy cluster must still be listed successfully.
body: Running `celery status` against a cluster whose broker is not reachable prints a raw Python traceback and exits with a generic failure code. Operators cannot tell whether they mistyped the broker URL, whether the broker is down, or whether they hit a bug in the tool. A command that cannot reach the cluster should report that as an unavailable service: exit with the platform's EX_UNAVAILABLE status, print one line naming the underlying reason, and print no traceback. A reachable broker with no workers must keep the unavailable outcome it already reports, and a healthy cluster must still be listed successfully.
acceptance_hint: `celery status` against an unreachable broker exits EX_UNAVAILABLE, includes the transport's own reason text in its output and prints no traceback; a healthy cluster still exits 0.
